title: Everyday math
lead: Everyday sums, no calculator. What matters is doing it at the checkout and at the table too.
realWorldNote: Some days the mission will be real-life math: those are the ones that raise your rank.
estimatesEmpty: Before looking up a price or a fact, estimate it. You'll see how close you were here.

problems.groceries: At the checkout you have: {{list}}. What's the total?
problems.tip: The bill is {{bill}}. How much is a {{pct}}% tip?
problems.split: The bill is {{total}} split evenly among {{people}} people. How much does each pay?
problems.discount: Something costs {{price}} with {{pct}}% off. How much do you pay?
problems.budget: Your monthly budget is {{budget}}. You've spent {{a}} on food, {{b}} on transport and {{c}} on fun. How much is left?
problems.travel: You need to cover {{km}} km at {{speed}} km/h. How many minutes does it take?
problems.recipe: A recipe for {{base}} people uses {{grams}} g of {{ingredient}}. How many grams for {{target}}?

tips.groceries: Round each price to the unit, add up, then fix the cents at the end.
tips.tip: 10% is moving the decimal point one place. 20% is double that. 15% is 10% plus half of it.
tips.split: Divide the whole part first, then share out what's left.
tips.discount: Work out what you pay, not what you save: 25% off means paying three quarters.
tips.budget: Add up the expenses first and subtract once.
tips.travel: Km divided by km/h gives hours; multiply by 60. At 60 km/h, one km is one minute.
tips.recipe: Work out the amount per person and multiply by the new number of people.

doneInvite: Next time you pay for something, work out the total before you're told.
estimateLead: First say what you think; then look up the real figure. Estimating well is a muscle.
estimateQuestionHint: Something from your life you can check today.

ideas.idea1: How much is a kilo of coffee at your store?
ideas.idea2: How much did you spend on food this week?
ideas.idea3: How many minutes does it take you to get to work?
ideas.idea4: How much was last month's electricity bill?
ideas.idea5: How many steps do you take on a normal day?

nowCheck: Now look up the real figure: the receipt, the bill, the map, the store.
estimateGreat: Very close. Your sense of quantities is sharp.
estimateOk: Reasonable. With practice, that margin narrows.
estimateFar: Far off, and that's fine: now you have that figure as a reference.
